title: The Hurricane club on Claiborne Street
summary: He describes his small club with trios such as King Cole and Charles Brown, opened in 1943.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What was the name of it? The Hurricane. Yeah.

What was that? It was on Claybone Street, South Claybone, 3700 block. Yeah. So we had a very nice club there, and it was small, and we were getting this track, you know, music, you're tracking into the club. Yeah. And I got hooked up in the booking business, you see.

Well, we had most of all the famous stuff at that time. King Cole was famous then. We had his trill in there. Charles Brown was famous. We had his trill in there. We had another group called Cat in the Field. They was famous in those times. Cat in the Field, yeah. Uh-huh. Lou Mel Morgan, he had a trill. See, we only had trill because the place was small, you see. Right.
How many people would it exist?
A whole about 200, Jim Moise. Right. But it was real fabulous. It was about the status of the city of New Orleans at that time.
